description: PF7 paging backward from page 3 to page 2 over the twenty-five-record file - the ONLY case that reaches the SUBTRACT at app/cbl/COUSR00C.cbl:367, and therefore the only witness of one of the four arithmetic sites gate G28 enumerates (:304, :358, the :309-310 and :320-321 pair, and :367 with its :369 ELSE). ENTRY. EIBCALEN is 194 and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives 1, so :115's NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is FALSE: :117 MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COUSR0AO never runs, :121 RECEIVEs the map and the EVALUATE EIBAID at :122-137 selects WHEN DFHPF7 at :128-129. That is why every span of the image below is SPACES and not one of them is LOW-VALUES - the distinction case02 to case05 exercise from the other side, and the one most easily normalised away (practices B5, B8). ANCHOR. CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST arrives ZUSER011, the first record of page 3, so :239's test against SPACES OR LOW-VALUES is false and :242 moves it into SEC-USR-ID: the browse is anchored on what the payload carried and on nothing a server remembered (rule R6, gate G37). :245 SETs NEXT-PAGE-YES unconditionally - correct, because the page being left is itself a page ahead - :246 places the cursor, and :248 finds CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM = 3 > 1, so :249 performs PROCESS-PAGE-BACKWARD rather than the already-at-the-top ELSE at :250-255 that case08 pins. THE BACKWARD PASS. :338's STARTBR on ZUSER011 reports NORMAL, so :340's IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON admits the rest of the paragraph - and this is the deliberate counterpart to case19, where a forced WHEN OTHER at :607-613 raises the error flag and the whole body INCLUDING its ENDBR is skipped. Here the ENDBR at :374 IS issued. :342 is COBOL's abbreviated combined relation EIBAID NOT = DFHENTER AND DFHPF8, which names TWO operands where :288 names three; PF7 is neither of them, so the relation holds and the READPREV at :343 discards ZUSER011, the record page 3 had already displayed. Keeping it would shift the whole page by one record. :346-350 then blanks all ten rows through INITIALIZE-USER-DATA at :446-501, which touches USRIDnnI, FNAMEnnI, LNAMEnnI and UTYPEnnI only and never SEL0001I to SEL0010I - so the selection column below is the blank the RECEIVE delivered rather than a cleared one. :352 MOVEs 10 to WS-IDX and the loop at :354-360 descends: READPREV, POPULATE-USER-DATA at the current subscript, then COMPUTE WS-IDX = WS-IDX - 1 at :358. Eleven READPREVs in all - one to discard the anchor and ten to fill - put ZUSER010 in row 10 and ZUSER001 in row 1, the exact opposite of the ascending forward fill case02 pins, while the blanking loop at :347 still ascends. POPULATE-USER-DATA's second receivers do the rest: WHEN 1 at :388-389 sets CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST to ZUSER001 and WHEN 10 at :433-435 sets CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST to ZUSER010 - the one-based OCCURS subscript, which is the top off-by-one risk of this migration. THE PAGE COUNT, ARGUED FROM THE SOURCE TEXT. :372's END-IF closes the IF opened at :362, so :363-371 are nested inside it even though the source indentation puts :363 and :364 in the same column as :362; reading them as siblings is the easiest misreading available here and it changes the answer. :362's IF USER-SEC-NOT-EOF AND ERR-FLG-OFF holds, because the fill ended on the subscript reaching zero rather than on end of file and no arm raised the flag. So :363's look-behind READPREV runs, returns USER0005 - the record below ZUSER001 - and reports NORMAL. :364's IF NEXT-PAGE-YES holds because :245 set it. :365-366's three-part condition therefore holds too: still not end of file, still no error, and CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM > 1 with the value 3. :367 consequently SUBTRACTs 1 and the count becomes 2 - NOT the 1 that :369's ELSE moves, which case20 pins by driving the look-behind into ENDFILE below ADMIN001. CLOSE AND SEND. :374 issues the ENDBR, :376 MOVEs CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM into PAGENUMI - PIC 9(08) into PIC X(8), so eight zero-padded digits, 00000002 - and :377 sends the map. PROCESS-PAGE-BACKWARD has no counterpart to :328's MOVE SPACE TO USRIDINO, so USRIDINO here is simply the eight spaces the RECEIVE delivered. Exactly ONE transmission is pinned: SEND-USRLST-SCREEN is reached from :119, :254, :276, :329, :377, :606, :613, :640, :647, :674 and :681, and only :377 lies on this path - MAIN-PARA's :119 belongs to the first-entry branch - so control returns from :249 straight to the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CU00') COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) of :141-144. SEND-ERASE-YES is still true from :103, because nothing on this path reaches the SET SEND-ERASE-NO of :253 or :275, so the send takes the ERASE arm at :529-535 and not the commented-out-ERASE arm at :537-543 that case08 and case09 pin. WS-MESSAGE was set to SPACES at :105 and no arm on this path moves anything into it, so :526's MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO leaves the message line at 78 spaces - which is an assertion and not the absence of one: this case is the READPREV NORMAL witness of gate G47's matrix, whose ENDFILE arm at :668-674 is case20's and whose WHEN OTHER arm at :675-681 is case17's. The matching READNEXT arms are witnessed elsewhere by construction - ENDFILE at :634-640 by case03 and case18, and WHEN OTHER at :641-647 by case10, where a HIGH-VALUES anchor makes the STARTBR performed at :284 report NOTFND at :600-606, so that the READNEXT at :289 - the one :288 guards - is issued against a browse never established. Neither can also be carried here, and the reason is a property of the frozen contract rather than a choice: ParityCase.ForcedOutcome declares outcome, resp and resp2 and NO call ordinal, so 'the fourth READNEXT fails' cannot be stated at all, the harness refuses a forced outcome no call site consumes, and this screen's projection reports exactly one image per invocation. Recorded rather than worked around silently (practice B4). STATE. All twenty-two communication-area fields are pinned: the sixteen of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, whose spans at :21-44 sum to 160, and the six of the 34-byte CDEMO-CU00-INFO extension declared beneath the COPY at :67-75 as 8+8+8+1+1+8. The extension is NOT a member of the shared common.NavigationContext, which stays exactly 160 for all seventeen online programs, so 194 is the whole area this transaction passes - and COTRN00C's CDEMO-CT00-INFO is 58, which must never be copied to it. CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT returns 1 and nothing on this path writes CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM, so the response names no next program and terminates on RETURN TRANSID rather than the XCTL of case01, case11, case13, case14 and case15 - the five that paint nothing at all. SEED. USRSEC has no ASCII fixture - app/data/ASCII holds nine and none of them is a security-user file - so its rows are always inline, and no tenth fixture file is introduced. The first ten are VERBATIM in-stream records of app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 at their in-stream width of exactly 57 characters; the fifteen ZUSER001 to ZUSER015 records after them are SYNTHESIZED so the file runs past two pages, and their keys sort after both ADMIN and USER so the file stays in ascending key order and the ten real records remain page 1. No row is pre-padded: the 23-byte shortfall is CSUSR01Y's absent SEC-USR-FILLER and it is carried to 80 exactly once, at seed time, by the single USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 normalisation declared below, whose sole owner is ParityCase.DatasetNormalisation.normaliseSeedRow, which ParityHarness calls. SEC-USR-PWD stays the plaintext eight-character literal the legacy design stores and app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl compares (practice B6); hashing, masking or omitting it would change what this contract asserts. FINAL STATE. The browse mutates nothing, so all twenty-five rows are pinned BOTH field by field - the six app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy spans in declaration order, with SEC-USR-FILLER NAMED because :23 names it rather than declaring an anonymous FILLER - AND as the whole 80-byte image, so the values, the total width and the filler having been emitted as spaces rather than zeros are each asserted (gates G17, G19, G21). The offsets are summed mechanically (practice B11): 8+20+20+8+1 = 57, plus X(23) makes 80, which is the LRECL=80 of DUSRSECJ.jcl:48 and the RECORDSIZE(80,80) of its IDCAMS DEFINE CLUSTER with KEYS(8,0) at :64-66. expectedDatasets then adds the count no row expectation can make, that USRSEC still holds exactly twenty-five rows at an 80-byte layout, and expectedWrites is empty as the positive assertion that a browse-only screen wrote nothing: app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:88-99 grants ADD, BROWSE, DELETE, READ and UPDATE on FILE(USRSEC) and this program uses browse alone. expectedReturnCode is 0, as for all twenty cases - COUSR00C contains no MOVE ... TO RETURN-CODE and no CALL 'CEE3ABD', and every path ends at :141-144 - and expectedMessages is empty because this program's fingerprint carries its message line inside the transmission rather than on a message channel, while the DISPLAY sites at :608, :642 and :676 are WHEN OTHER arms this path never reaches. CONVENTIONS, matching case01 exactly. jobParameters is OMITTED rather than declared empty, because ParityCase refuses a job parameter for any unitKind but BATCH_JOB and the conversation scalars travel as screenRequest.eibcalen, screenRequest.aid and screenRequest.commarea instead. The code page is named US-ASCII explicitly and never defaulted (practice B8). The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34, the source's own version stamp at :694 rather than an invented instant, because POPULATE-HEADER-INFO calls FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE at :564 on every send and an unpinned header would make the CURDATEO of :575 and the CURTIMEO of :581 irreproducible (practice B7). USRSEC is addressed by its binding key throughout and never by a dataset name (gate G46). Page size ten is BEHAVIOUR and not configuration (gate G39): it is hard-coded at :293, :300, :347 and :352 and by 02 USER-REC OCCURS 10 TIMES at :57, and no page-size value appears anywhere in this file. The WS-USER-DATA array at :56-64 is dead - no paragraph reads or writes it - and stays unmodelled (practice B5). COUSR00C does not COPY CSSTRPFY or CSSETATY: its COPY list at :66-84 is COCOM01Y, COUSR00, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CSUSR01Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA, so no runtime DFHRED and no '*' overwrite exists to be invented - ERRMSG is statically COLOR=RED in app/bms/COUSR00.bms. RULE R1: the plan mandates the class name UserMenuController, but :5 reads 'List all users from USRSEC file', app/bms/COUSR00.bms paints 'List Users' and README.md records CU00 the same way; the name comes from the plan and the behaviour from the source, so nothing here expects menu-shaped behaviour. PROVENANCE (practice B12, risk R-A, AAP 0.7.6 and 0.9.11): every expected value above was DERIVED BY STRUCTURED READING of the COBOL and its copybooks and was NOT captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy program - executing it is impossible in this environment, which has no z/OS or CICS runtime, whose COBOL compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, which offers no Language Environment CEE* services, and which is missing the IBM-supplied DFHAID and DFHBMSCA this program COPYs at :83-84. Only the provenance of the expected values is substituted; the twenty cases per program, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-of-zero gate per module are all preserved. The derivation rests on app/cbl/COUSR00C.cbl:50-51, :56-75, :98-144, :237-255, :336-379, :384-441, :446-501, :522-545, :562-581 and :653-681; app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:19-44; app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23; app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-22, whose CCDA-TITLE01 and CCDA-TITLE02 are the two 40-character literals pinned above; app/cpy-bms/COUSR00.CPY, whose xxxI items give every payload field its width while its xxxL, xxxF and xxxA items stay metadata; app/bms/COUSR00.bms, whose 89 DFHMDF definitions comprise the 59 NAMED fields pinned above and 30 unnamed literals that carry no payload; and app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, :48 and :64-66.
